what: Soil type, available water capacity through the bean root zone, slope and drainage, sampled at the centre of every bean cell and aggregated by region on bean acres.
why: Every water figure on this site used one invented root-zone capacity of 120 mm for all seven regions. These are the measured capacities instead, and the slopes that decide how much rain stays where it falls.
root_zone_source: FAO-56 Table 22 gives 0.5-0.7 m effective rooting depth for green and dry beans; 60 cm is the middle of that published range.

source.name: USDA NRCS Soil Data Access (SSURGO) — the official soil survey of the United States, surveyed on the ground

limits: A point sample at the centre of each cell. Where a cell straddles two map units it takes the one under its middle.
The dominant major component of each map unit stands for the whole unit.
A region figure is an average over hundreds of cells and is not anyone's field.
Available water capacity is what the soil can hold, not what is in it today.
